hindi: पके हुए, पुराने अथवा सूखे जीमूतक फलों का चूर्ण वातपित्त में।
english: The powder of the ripe, old, or dried fruits of jīmūtaka, in vātapitta.
notes: No verb is given; the earlier unit's verb of application (prayojayet) is understood. paryāgata taken as 'fully come (ripe)'; vātapitta read as the joint Vāta-Pitta condition.

words.gloss: of those beginning with āragvadha (drug name)

hindi: दो या तीन फलों को कूटकर, आरग्वध आदि ताज़े द्रव्यों में से किसी एक के अथवा पटोली के काढ़े में भिगोकर, मथकर, पित्त और कफ से उत्पन्न ज्वर में।
english: Two or three (of them), crushed, steeped in the decoction of any one of the fresh ones beginning with āragvadha or of paṭolī, and churned, in fever (jvara) born of Pitta and phlegm.

text_flags.why: possible: the neuter plural of tri is trīṇi, so dvitrāṇi looks like a damaged form

notes: Doubts: (1) navānām: 'fresh' chosen as the plainest sense; 'nine' is possible. (2) āsuta (from ā-√su) glossed 'steeped'; the exact sense is unsure. (3) The thing crushed is not named (probably the jīmūtaka fruits of the previous unit). Glossary OPEN item: niryūha, kaṣāya, kvātha all rendered 'decoction' (Hindi काढ़ा) throughout this chunk.

hindi: जीमूतक का चूर्ण अथवा कल्क ठंडे जल के साथ, पित्त से उत्पन्न में।
english: Jīmūtaka powder or paste with cold water, in what is born of Pitta.
notes: The noun for 'what is born of Pitta' (probably jvara, as in unit 38) is not stated.

hindi: वही गरम जल के साथ, वात और कफ से उत्पन्न में अथवा कफ से उत्पन्न में।
english: That same, with warm (water), in what is born of Vāta and Kapha, or of Kapha.
notes: 'water' is understood from the previous unit.

words.gloss: of jīvaka, ṛṣabhaka, ikṣu and śatāvarī (drug names)

hindi: जीवक, ऋषभक, इक्षु और शतावरी में से किसी एक के स्वरस के साथ, पित्त से उत्पन्न में।
english: With the expressed juice of any one of jīvaka, ṛṣabhaka, ikṣu and śatāvarī, in what is born of Pitta.
notes: Genitive plural followed by genitive singular anyatamasya ('of any one of them'). ikṣu is kept as a name.

hindi: अथवा पहले की भाँति पकाया हुआ घृत।
english: Or ghee cooked as before.
notes: 'As before' refers back to an earlier preparation; not named here.

words.gloss: in kāsa (cough), śvāsa (breath-trouble), jvara (fever), chardi (vomiting), viṣa (poison) and phlegm-ailments

hindi: इक्ष्वाकु तो विशेष रूप से कास, श्वास, ज्वर, छर्दि, विष और कफ के रोगों में प्रयोग करने योग्य है।
english: Ikṣvāku, however, is especially to be applied in kāsa (cough), śvāsa (laboured breathing), jvara (fever), chardi (vomiting), viṣa (poison) and phlegm-ailments.

text_flags.why: possible: long ī here, but the same word is spelled with short i in units 45 to 55 (variant spelling or scan error)

notes: The final member -roga may govern all the preceding members (as translated) or only śleṣma.

words.gloss: in one whose Pitta is excessive
in fever of Pitta and Kapha
in the flowers and the rest

hindi: उसके, पुष्प और फल से रहित अवस्था के, नवपल्लवों के साथ उबाला हुआ दूध, जिसमें पित्त बढ़ा हो उसमें और पित्त तथा कफ के ज्वर में; किन्तु पुष्प आदि में प्रयोग रात-जीमूत के समान हैं।
english: Milk boiled with the sprouts of that one while it is without flower and fruit, in one whose Pitta is excessive and in fever of Pitta and Kapha; but in the case of the flowers and the rest, the applications are like those of rāta-jīmūta.

text_flags.why: 'heard' makes no sense with milk; ṛ/u confusion in the scan, śṛta = boiled
rāta is not a known word here; possible damage (perhaps a lost or altered word before jīmūtavat); kept as printed

notes: Doubtful: (1) rātajīmūtavat: reading unclear, translation follows the printed letters. (2) 'that one' (tasya) is the ikṣvāku of the previous passage. (3) a-puṣpa-phala could also mean 'not yet flowered or fruited'.

words.gloss: expressed juice of the ikṣvāku fruit

hindi: अथवा इक्ष्वाकु के फल का स्वरस, तिगुने दूध में पकाया हुआ, वमन चाहने वाला रोगी पित्त में, कफ-पीनस में और स्वरसाद में पिए।
english: Or the patient, desiring emesis, should drink the expressed juice of the ikṣvāku fruit prepared in threefold milk, in Pitta, in kapha-pīnasa and in svarasāda.
notes: triguṇa-kṣīra: 'milk three times (the quantity)' is the plain sense; the exact measure is not stated. pibeta is a middle-voice optative, kept as printed.

words.gloss: from which the seeds are taken out

hindi: अथवा पके हुए, बीज निकाले हुए फल में दूध डाले।
english: Or one should pour milk into a ripe fruit from which the seeds have been taken out.

words.gloss: in phlegm-kāsa, śvāsa, aruci (distaste for food) and chardi

hindi: उसमें बना हुआ दही कफ के कास, श्वास, अरुचि और छर्दि में।
english: The curd formed in it, in phlegm-kāsa, śvāsa, aruci (distaste for food) and chardi.

text_flags.why: śvāsa + aruc requires ā (śvāsāruc-); printed u is a likely scan error

notes: śleṣmakāsa is read as 'kāsa of phlegm'; it could also be two separate members (phlegm; kāsa).

words.gloss: in viṣa (poison), gulma (lump), udara (belly-ailment), galagaṇḍa (neck-swelling), granthi (knot), arbuda (growth) and ślīpada

hindi: अथवा बकरी के दूध में भिगोए हुए इक्ष्वाकु के बीज, विष, गुल्म, उदर, गलगण्ड, ग्रन्थि, अर्बुद और श्लीपद में।
english: Or ikṣvāku seeds soaked in she-goat's milk, in viṣa (poison), gulma (lump), udara (belly-ailment), galagaṇḍa (neck-swelling), granthi (knot), arbuda (growth) and ślīpada.
notes: Disease terms are given by their plain literal senses only; udara here is an ailment term, not just 'belly'.

words.gloss: inner part of the ikṣvāku fruit
in kuṣṭha, viṣa, gulma, udara, gara (concocted poison), gaṇḍa (swelling), granthi, arbuda and ślīpada

hindi: अथवा इक्ष्वाकु फल का मध्य भाग, कुष्ठ, विष, गुल्म, उदर, गर, गण्ड, ग्रन्थि, अर्बुद और श्लीपद में।
english: Or the inner part of the ikṣvāku fruit, in kuṣṭha, viṣa, gulma, udara, gara (concocted poison), gaṇḍa (swelling), granthi, arbuda and ślīpada.
notes: The printed udara-gara-gaṇḍa could be a damaged 'udara-gala-gaṇḍa' (compare unit 48); kept as printed (gara and gaṇḍa as separate members), and gara is a regular term in units 60 and 65.

hindi: इक्ष्वाकु फल मस्तु के साथ, कुष्ठ, विष और पाण्डु रोगों में।
english: Ikṣvāku fruit with whey, in kuṣṭha, viṣa and pale-ailments (pāṇḍvāmaya).
notes: pāṇḍu rendered 'pale' per the glossary; āmaya 'ailment'. mastu = whey (watery part of curds).

hindi: अथवा सद्रिपक, या मधु और सैंधव सहित तक्र।
english: Or sadripaka; or buttermilk with honey and saindhava.

text_flags.why: not a recognisable word (possibly sa- 'with' plus a damaged noun); kept as printed

notes: sadripaka is not understood; it may be a damaged word. The vā may join sadripaka and takra as alternatives (as translated), or sadripaka may qualify takra ('buttermilk together with sadripaka'). saindhava glossed 'salt' as it names a kind of salt.

hindi: अथवा वही मध्य भाग, एक पल गुड़ सहित, खाए।
english: Or one should eat that same inner part together with a pala of jaggery.
notes: saguḍapalam could also mean 'with jaggery (and) a pala' (a pala of what is not clear); pala is a unit of weight.

hindi: अथवा इक्ष्वाकु फल का तेल पिए।
english: Or one should drink the oil of the ikṣvāku fruit.

words.gloss: soaked in the expressed juice of that fruit
in phlegm-fever, kāsa, throat-ailments and arocaka (distaste for food)

hindi: अथवा उसी फल के स्वरस में भिगोए हुए सत्तुओं के साथ मन्थ, कफ के ज्वर, कास, कण्ठ के रोगों और अरोचक में।
english: Or a mantha (stirred drink) with saktu (parched-grain flour) steeped in the expressed juice of that same fruit, in phlegm-fever, kāsa, throat-ailments and arocaka (distaste for food).

text_flags.why: possible: printed -bhāvitaiva does not agree with saktubhiḥ; inst. pl. bhāvitaiḥ + eva (bhāvitair eva) fits, with r lost in the scan

notes: The reading bhāvitaiva is doubtful; the repair bhāvitaiḥ eva is a guess. Alternatively bhāvitā eva (fem.) with an unstated feminine noun.

words.gloss: in Vāta-Kapha, gulma and persistent fevers

hindi: इक्ष्वाकु का कल्क मांस के रस के साथ, वात-कफ, गुल्म और लगे रहने वाले ज्वरों में।
english: Ikṣvāku paste with meat broth, in Vāta-Kapha, gulma and persistent fevers.
notes: The compound can also be read 'in persistent fevers of Vāta, Kapha and gulma'. prasakta = 'attached, persistent'.

words.gloss: with a decoction of a prastha of bilva root

hindi: अथवा एक प्रस्थ बिल्व की जड़ के काढ़े में तुम्बी के बीज उबाले।
english: Or one should boil tumbī seeds in a decoction of a prastha of bilva root.

text_flags.why: k-v ligature lost; kvātha = decoction
kādhayet is not a word; kvāthayet 'should boil' fits the sense

notes: prastha is a measure; whether it measures the root or the decoction is not clear.

words.gloss: in which the ghee is a third part
jīmūta, mahājālinī, vatsaka and kṛtavedhana (drug names)
trikaṭuka (set of three, lit. three pungent)

hindi: तत्पश्चात् उसमें, जिसमें घृत तीसरा भाग है, घृत के बराबर पीसे हुए तुम्बी के बीज, और उनके आधे अंश वाले जीमूत, महाजालिनी, वत्सक और कृतवेधन प्रत्येक, तथा काढ़े के बराबर त्रिकटु डाले।
english: Then, into that, in which the ghee is a third part, one should add tumbī seeds ground equal to the ghee, and, each at half that portion, jīmūta, mahājālinī, vatsaka and kṛtavedhana, and trikaṭuka equal to the decoction.

text_flags.why: anusvāra lost: aṃśika 'having a portion' is needed
short u for ū in jīmūta (possible)

notes: Doubtful: (1) tribhāga taken as 'a third part' (could be 'three parts'). (2) tad-ardha-aṃśika: 'half that quantity'; which members are meant to be at half the quantity is a judgement from pratyekam. (3) 'trikaṭuka equal to the decoction' is literal; the odd quantity is not corrected here. (4) the base liquid is the decoction of unit 56.

hindi: तत्पश्चात् फिर भी पकाकर लेह तैयार करे।
english: Then, having boiled it again, one should prepare a leha (licked preparation).

text_flags.why: śrutvā means 'having heard'; sense needs 'having boiled'; the exact original form (śṛtvā, śrātvā or śrapayitvā) is uncertain

notes: The corrected form and its root are uncertain; sense 'having boiled' follows unit 44 (śṛtam). Glossary OPEN item (literal verbs for lehayet etc.) not triggered in this unit.

words.gloss: in those beginning with kāśmarya (drug name)
in the members of the great five roots

hindi: उसे चाटकर पीछे प्रमथ्या पिए, और उसी प्रकार घृत भी; यह कल्प काश्मर्य आदि चार महापञ्चमूल के अंगों में अलग-अलग कहा हुआ जानना चाहिए।
english: Having licked it, one should drink a pramathyā afterwards, and likewise ghee; the procedure (kalpa) is to be understood as stated separately in each of the four members of the great five roots, beginning with kāśmarya.

text_flags.why: possible: dh for th in pramathyā; and -ddham looks like ddhṛtam (ṛt lost): 'likewise ghee'
second suggestion for the same token: ghṛtam with the ṛ lost (compare pūrvavaddhṛtaṃ, unit 42)

notes: Doubtful: pramathyā and the ghee are conjectural repairs; the ending of the sentence (the 'four members of the great five roots') is taken literally and not explained.

words.gloss: in gara (concocted poison), gulma, udara, kāsa and ailments arising from accumulation of Kapha
located in the seat of phlegm

hindi: धामार्गव विशेष रूप से गर, गुल्म, उदर, कास तथा कफ के संचय से उत्पन्न रोगों में, जो स्थिर और भारी हों उनमें, कफ के आशय में स्थित रोगों में, और कण्ठ में आश्रय वाले वात-कफ में।
english: Dhāmārgava, especially in gara, gulma, udara, kāsa and the ailments arising from an accumulation of Kapha; in those that are firm and heavy, in those located in the seat of phlegm, and in Vāta-phlegm whose seat is the throat.

text_flags.why: anusvāra after dhā is probably an error (dhāmārgava in units 62 to 64)

notes: sthireṣu and guruṣu are taken to qualify the ailments (rogeṣu). The end of the unit has no verb of application.

words.gloss: joined with powder of any one of the jīvanīya group

hindi: जीवनीय गण में से किसी एक के चूर्ण से युक्त, मधु और शर्करा सहित, उन्हीं के काढ़ों से लेह तैयार करके, पित्त के गौण होने पर कफ की अवस्था में प्रयोग करे।
english: Having prepared lehas (licked preparations) joined with the powder of any one of the jīvanīya (life-promoting) group, with honey and sugar, and made with decoctions of those, one should prescribe them in the phlegm condition in which Pitta is secondary.
notes: tat-kaṣāyaiḥ: 'their decoctions' is taken as the decoctions of the drugs just named. upasarjana literally 'accompaniment, subordinate'.

words.gloss: with a broth of tumbaru and dhānya

hindi: धामार्गव का कल्क तुम्बरु और धान्य के यूष के साथ, विषों में।
english: Dhāmārgava paste with a broth of tumbaru and dhānya, in poisons.

text_flags.why: viṣedhu is not a word; viṣeṣu 'in poisons' fits the sense (ṣu/dhu confusion)

notes: dhānya is literally 'grain' and may here be a drug name; kept as a name in the translation.

hindi: सुमनः, सौमनस्या, यवानी, हरिद्रा, चोरक, हैमवती, महासहा, क्षुद्रसहा, वृश्चीव, अर्बी के बीज, पुनर्नवा और कासमर्द में से किसी एक के काढ़े के साथ, अथवा एक या दो धामार्गव, मन के विकारों में।
english: With the decoction of any one of sumanas, saumanasyā, yavānī, haridrā, coraka, haimavatī, mahāsahā, kṣudrasahā, vṛścīva, arbī seeds, punarnavā and kāsamarda, or one or two of dhāmārgava, in disorders of the mind.
notes: Doubtful: the split of the long compound (especially vṛścīva-arbī-bīja: sandhi a+a, but arbī is unknown, so the member may be damaged or the division different, e.g. vṛścī + vārbī) and saumanasyā as a drug name. 'one or two' dhāmārgava: the thing counted is not stated (fruit, part?). All names kept untranslated.

words.gloss: produced from milk cooked with dhāmārgava root
cooked with the six beginning with phala

hindi: धामार्गव की जड़ से सिद्ध किए हुए दूध से उत्पन्न घृत, अथवा फल आदि छह से सिद्ध घृत, मन के विकारों में।
english: Ghee produced from milk cooked with the root of dhāmārgava, or ghee cooked with the six beginning with phala, in disorders of the mind.
notes: 'the six beginning with phala' (phalādi-ṣaṭ) is a group not listed here; the translation stays literal.

words.gloss: in gara, udara, gulma, plīha (spleen), pale-ailments (pāṇḍu-roga) and swelling (śvayathu)

hindi: कृतवेधन, अत्यन्त कटु, तीक्ष्ण और उष्ण, विशेष रूप से गर, उदर, गुल्म, प्लीहा, पाण्डु रोग और शोथ में तैयार करे।
english: One should prepare kṛtavedhana, exceedingly pungent, sharp and hot, especially for gara, udara, gulma, plīha (spleen), pale-ailments (pāṇḍu-roga) and swelling (śvayathu).
notes: kalpayet 'should prepare, arrange' (for use). kaṭu = pungent, acrid.

words.gloss: in those in whom blood, Pitta and Kapha are prominent
in vātaśoṇita, visarpa, jvara, kuṣṭha and the rest

hindi: कुटज का फल फिर सुकुमार व्यक्तियों में, जिनमें रक्त, पित्त और कफ प्रबल हों उनमें, और वातशोणित, विसर्प, ज्वर, कुष्ठ आदि में प्रयोग करे।
english: One should apply kuṭaja fruit, on the other hand, in delicate persons, in those in whom blood, Pitta and Kapha are prominent, and in vātaśoṇita, visarpa, jvara, kuṣṭha and the rest.
notes: ulbaṇa-rakta-pitta-kapha could also be read as 'prominent raktapitta and Kapha'; visarpa 'spreading'; vātaśoṇita 'wind-blood'. Kept literal.

words.gloss: with the decoction of any one of the madanaphala, jīmūtaka, ikṣvāku, jīvantī and jīvaka roots
words.gram: m. inst. sg., dvandva and tat-puruṣa

words.gloss: with water of any one of sarṣapa, madhūka and salt

hindi: कुटज फल के चूर्णों को अर्क के दूध से सात दिन तक भिगोकर, अथवा मदनफल, जीमूतक, इक्ष्वाकु, जीवन्ती और जीवक की जड़ों में से किसी एक के काढ़े से, अथवा सर्षप, मधूक और लवण में से किसी एक के जल से, अथवा कुटज फल का चूर्ण कृशरा के साथ, वमन के लिए तैयार करे। ऐसा।
english: Having soaked kuṭaja fruit powders for seven days in the milk of arka, or in the decoction of any one of the madanaphala, jīmūtaka, ikṣvāku, jīvantī and jīvaka roots, or in water of any one of sarṣapa, madhūka and salt, or kuṭaja fruit powder with kṛśarā, one should prepare it for emesis. Thus.

text_flags.why: extra anusvāra: cūrṇāni + arka gives cūrṇānyarka
short u and extra anusvāra: mūla + anyatama gives mūlānyatama
krū for kṛ; kṛśarā is the known word

notes: Doubtful: (1) whether 'mūla' governs all the names before it (as translated) or only jīvaka. (2) sarṣapa and madhūka kept as drug names; lavaṇa 'salt'. (3) 'iti' closes the passage and is rendered 'Thus'. (4) The grammar of the 'or with' alternatives (what is prepared) is elliptical.

hindi: और इस विषय में यह है।
english: And here there is this:
notes: Lead-in formula introducing the verse in units 69 and 70. GROUPING: units 68, 69 and 70 belong together (formula, then one verse of two half-verse lines). 'this' (the verse that follows) is understood.

hindi: यह वमनों का, विशेष रूप से उपयोगी वमनों का, निर्देश है।
english: This is the indication of emetics, of those especially useful.

text_flags.why: nā lost: genitive plural vamanānām is needed for the sense and the 8-syllable line

notes: GROUPING: this unit is the first half-verse of a verse completed by unit 70 (68 is its lead-in). Doubtful: the final upayoginām has no noun; taken as 'of the useful ones' (emetics).

hindi: इस बीज से बुद्धिमान अन्यों की भी कल्पना करे।
english: With this as a seed, the wise one should devise variations on others also.

text_flags.why: possible: anyān + api gives anyānapi; the anusvāra is probably a scan error

notes: GROUPING: this unit is the second half-verse completing the verse begun in unit 69. 'seed' (bīja) is used figuratively: the model from which variations may be made.

hindi: इस प्रकार वमनकल्प नामक प्रथम अध्याय।
english: Thus (ends) the first chapter, named Vamanakalpa (preparations for emesis).
notes: Chapter colophon.
